definition: A mathematical framework for quantifying and limiting the privacy risk to individuals whose data is used in training or analysis, typically by adding calibrated noise.
details: Differential privacy provides formal guarantees that the presence or absence of any single individual's data has limited effect on a model's output, helping protect against training-data extraction or membership-inference attacks.
story: Picture a parachute packed by a second pair of hands: nobody plans to need it, but everyone is glad it was checked. Think of it this way: A mathematical framework for quantifying and limiting the privacy risk to individuals whose data is used in training or analysis, typically by adding calibrated noise. And here is the clever part: Differential privacy provides formal guarantees that the presence or absence of any single individual's data has limited effect on a model's output, helping protect against training-data extraction or membership-inference attacks. Caution is not the enemy of progress — it is the reason progress gets to keep going. And that is Differential Privacy — the reason we can move fast without breaking things, or people.
